land.text: the Jinhan confederacy's land: Silla 'began as Saro-guk, a statelet within the 12-member confederacy known as Jinhan'

predecessors.note: The page's founding date is 57 BCE ('based in myth'); Silla is on the map from 378 because the Jinhan dossier ends in 377, the year of the first emissaries to China.

land.text: Silla after the conquest of Baekje and of the land south of the Taedong River

successors.note: The same kingdom under the label 'Unified Silla' (Cliopatria opens a new row in 682).

capitals.name: Seorabeol (Gyeongju)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Seorabeol'; the Unified Silla page says Gyeongju 'remained the capital of Silla throughout the whole existence of the dynasty'.

keyframe_review.note: 23,506 km2, the Jinhan outline for 378-531. The page has no area; it dates the 12-member Jinhan confederacy to the origin of Silla ('Saro-guk'), Naemul (356-402) as the king who 'took the royal title of Maripgan', and 'In 377, Silla sent emissaries to China'. Sillan land beyond Gyeongsang is not described before 532. Fix round: Cliopatria draws this outline to 533, but the Jangsu of Goguryeo page has Jangsu 'expanding his domain into parts of Gangwon Province' in 468 and, in 489, 'capturing 7 walled cities and expanding his domain into parts of North Gyeongsang Province'; Cliopatria's Goguryeo outlines do not reach this land (0 shared cells), so the losses are written here (ledger) and drawn in silla_468, silla_489 and silla_532. Years change only for this shape. The Naemul of Silla page (opened for the 378 bridge) does not mention Jinhan or Saro-guk and gives no 378: the start year stays a confidence-1 bridge.

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria 378 shape; valid 378-467 (the Gangwon strip goes to Goguryeo in 468, the northern frontier of North Gyeongsang in 489)
Silla without the Gangwon part Goguryeo took in 468

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Jangsu invaded Silla in 468, expanding his domain into parts of Gangwon Province' (Jangsu of Goguryeo page). The part of Silla's outline that lies in Gangwon (14 grid cells, about 3,500 km2) is the researcher's reading, the same region as goguryeo /ledger/30; the page does not say how much Goguryeo held.

correction.text: Silla without the Gangwon part (468) and without the northern frontier strip of North Gyeongsang (489)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Jangsu invaded again 'in 489, capturing 7 walled cities and expanding his domain into parts of North Gyeongsang Province' (Jangsu of Goguryeo page). The page names no city; the 7 walled cities are drawn as the strip of North Gyeongsang within three grid cells (about 40 km) of Goguryeo's frontier (about 3,800 km2), the researcher's reading, not the whole province (23,000 km2, Gyeongju included) that goguryeo /ledger/33 intersects. Silla kept its capital Gyeongju.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 534 outline (with Geumgwan Gaya) minus the land Goguryeo took in 468 and 489

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Silla with Geumgwan Gaya from 532 ('conquered in 532'), still without the frontier land of 468 and 489. No page says when Silla recovered it; the first Silla campaign against Goguryeo on any page is 551 (Jinheung page), so the land is drawn back in Silla from 551 (silla_534 below), a confidence-1 bridge.

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria 534 shape; valid 551-553 (532-550 is silla_532, without the land lost in 468 and 489; the Han River gain comes in 553)

keyframe_review.note: 26,619 km2 (+3,113 km2): Geumgwan Gaya, which 'was conquered in 532' (the Gaya page also has Silla destroying Takgitan Gaya in 529 and taking half of Taksun Gaya, with no place named). Cliopatria starts two years late and runs to 554; the Han River gain comes in 553. Fix round: the shape is valid only from 551, when the frontier land of 468 and 489 is back in Silla (silla ledger, confidence 1); 532-550 is silla_532. Years change only.

75,507 km2 (+48,888 km2): the page has Silla in 553 'wrest[ing] control of the entire central western Korea region from Paekche' after 551 as an ally against Goguryeo (Jinheung page: attack on the Han River valley 'during the year 553', 'late 553' against the Baekje army). So the gain is real but starts in 554, not 555. The part of this shape reaching the east coast to 40.1 N (Hamgyong, 7,600 km2) is not on any page opened (fix round: the Three Kingdoms of Korea page is silent on Jinheung and the east coast, and the Jinheung and Silla pages again give no Hamgyong, Hwangchoryeong or Masikryeong): unverified. The Silla infobox lists 'Campaigns of King Jinheung: 551-585'.

86,616 km2 (+11,108 km2): Daegaya, 'conquered by Silla in 562' (Gaya page; the Jinheung page has Kim Isabu conquering it 'in 561'). Cliopatria starts five years late. The infobox gives no area. Years change only.

86,526 km2. In 660 Silla and Tang conquered Baekje (Unified Silla page: 'In 660, King Munmu ordered his armies to attack Baekje.' 'General Kim Yu-sin, aided by Tang forces, defeated General Gyebaek and conquered Baekje.') and the land was jointly occupied; Silla's own outline does not change until it 'drove Tang forces out of most of Baekje's former territory' in 671 (Silla-Tang War page).
86,616 km2. After 668 'Silla and Tang occupied Baekje and Goguryeo'; the outline holds only to 670, the year the Silla-Tang War starts. Years change only.

correction.text: Silla plus the former Baekje territory

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 671, Silla drove Tang forces out of most of Baekje's former territory.' Cliopatria draws the Baekje land in Silla only from 682. Goguryeo's south stays with Tang until 676.

correction.text: use silla_671 for 674-675 and the Unified Silla 682 shape (without Jeju) for 676-681

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 674-681 shape repeats the 567 outline although Silla held Baekje's land from 671 and the land south of the Taedong from 676: superseded by silla_671 (674-675) and silla_676 (676-681).

correction.text: Silla south of the Taedong River without Jeju

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Silla recaptured the territory south of Taedong River' (infobox, 670-676); afterwards 'Silla controlled most of the Korean Peninsula' with a line 'from the mouth of the Taedong River in the west to the East Korea Bay'. The Cliopatria 682 shape (149,880 km2) is that territory; Jeju is removed because the Tamna dossier keeps it as a Silla tributary.

region.text: Silla's core, the former Jinhan land of Gyeongsang

ledger.note: 378: Silla appears on the map, replacing the Jinhan outline. The page dates the founding to 57 BCE ('based in myth') and records only that 'In 377, Silla sent emissaries to China and established relations with Goguryeo' under Naemul (356-402); 378 is Cliopatria's start and the Jinhan dossier's handover. Fix round: the Naemul of Silla page (381 tribute mission to Early Jin, 392 alliance and vassalage to Goguryeo) is silent on Jinhan and on 378, so the year stays a confidence-1 bridge.

region.text: parts of Gangwon Province within Silla's outline

ledger.note: 468: Goguryeo takes the Gangwon edge of Silla. 'Jangsu invaded Silla in 468, expanding his domain into parts of Gangwon Province' (Jangsu of Goguryeo page). Mirror of goguryeo /ledger/30 (same region, 14 grid cells, about 3,500 km2). The year is the page's; how much land and for how long is the researcher's reading, since the page does not say whether Goguryeo kept it.

region.text: the northern frontier strip of North Gyeongsang, where the 7 walled cities lay (researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 489: Goguryeo takes 7 walled cities. 'and again in 489, capturing 7 walled cities and expanding his domain into parts of North Gyeongsang Province' (Jangsu of Goguryeo page). The page names no city and no area; the strip of North Gyeongsang within three grid cells of Goguryeo's border (about 3,800 km2) is the researcher's reading. goguryeo /ledger/33 intersects the whole province with Silla's outline (23,267 km2, Gyeongju included); that region should be narrowed to this one.

region.text: Geumgwan Gaya, at the mouth of the Nakdong

ledger.note: 532: Silla conquers Geumgwan Gaya. 'Geumgwan Gaya, the ruling state of the confederacy, was conquered in 532'; Silla had destroyed Takgitan Gaya in 529. Region is the Cliopatria step between the 533 and 534 Gaya shapes (the page names no territory).
551: Silla and Baekje attack Goguryeo. Jinheung 'allied with Baekje so that he could attack the northern Korean kingdom of Goguryeo' in 551; the Han River valley is fought over until 553.

region.text: the frontier land of Gangwon and North Gyeongsang that Goguryeo took in 468 and 489

ledger.note: 551 at the latest: Silla is back on its northern frontier. No page dates the recovery of the land lost in 468 and 489; the Jinheung page has Silla in 551 allying with Baekje 'so that he could attack the northern Korean kingdom of Goguryeo' and gives no district, so 551 is a bridge (the Silla outline of Cliopatria's 534 and 555 shapes holds the land again). goguryeo has no matching loss yet.

region.text: Silla's half of the conquered Han River valley, without the Seoul region (Gyeonggi), which Baekje holds from 551 and Silla takes only in 553

ledger.note: 551: Silla's share of the Han River conquest. 'The result was the conquest of the Han River estuary'; 'The kingdoms of Baekje and Silla agreed on splitting the conquered territory equally between themselves' (undated on the page). Which half was Silla's is the researcher's reading: the upper valley, the Baekje half being the Seoul region, which is subtracted here (fix round: the whole 554-to-555 step also held Gyeonggi, 14,000 km2, which baekje gains from Goguryeo in 551 and this dossier takes from Baekje in 553).

region.text: the central western Korea region, Baekje's share of the Han River valley

ledger.note: 553: Silla takes the whole Han River region from Baekje. 'Silla wrested control of the entire central western Korea region from Paekche', 'breaching the 120-year Paekche-Silla alliance' (Silla page); Jinheung page: Silla troops attacked 'the exhausted Baekje army in late 553', King Seong was killed in 554.

553: the Han River fighting ends with Silla in possession ('launched an attack on the Han River valley during the year 553'); Baekje's counterattack and King Seong's death in 554 are a separate episode.

region.text: the last holdout Daegaya and the remaining Gaya polities

ledger.note: 562: Daegaya falls and Gaya ends. 'Daegaya ... conquered by Silla in 562, as punishment for assisting Paekche' (Gaya page; the Jinheung page says Kim Isabu conquered it 'in 561'). Region is Cliopatria's last Gaya outline.

660: Silla and Tang conquer Baekje. 'In 660, King Munmu ordered his armies to attack Baekje.' 'General Kim Yu-sin, aided by Tang forces, defeated General Gyebaek and conquered Baekje.' (Unified Silla page); 'After the Goguryeo-Tang War ended in 668, Silla and Tang occupied Baekje and Goguryeo' (Silla-Tang War page). Hatched until Silla drives the Tang out in 671.

region.text: Jeju Island, the kingdom of Tamna

ledger.note: 662: Tamna becomes Silla's tributary. Tamna infobox 'Tributary state of Silla (662-925)'; the text says only that 'near the end of the Three Kingdoms period, Tamna officially subjugated itself to Silla'.

region.text: former Baekje and the Goguryeo lands south of the Taedong

ledger.note: 670: the Silla-Tang War begins. Infobox 'Date: 670-676'; 'From 670 to 673 the rebels launched an uprising every year' and Silla sided with the Goguryeo loyalists. The zone matches the Tang dossier's.
671: Silla expels the Tang from Baekje. 'In 671, Silla drove Tang forces out of most of Baekje's former territory.'
671: Baekje's old land is Silla's. 'In 671, Silla drove Tang forces out of most of Baekje's former territory.'

region.text: the territory south of the Taedong River

ledger.note: 676: Silla wins the war. 'Silla recaptured the territory south of Taedong River'; 'a Silla victory at Gibeolpo in November' 676; Tang moved the Protectorate General to Pacify the East from Pyongyang to Liaoyang (676) and then Xincheng (677).

region.text: the territory south of the Taedong River, formerly Goguryeo's

ledger.note: 676: Silla holds the peninsula south of the Taedong. 'Silla recaptured the territory south of Taedong River, while Tang held control over former Goguryeo territory north of Taedong River'; Tang formally recognised this in 736.
681: the Silla dossier ends; Tamna's tribute continues in the Unified Silla dossier (to 925, Tamna infobox). Closing event so the start and end pair inside the file.

region.text: all of Silla, passing to the same kingdom under the new label

ledger.note: 681: Silla continues as 'Unified Silla'. Same kingdom, new Cliopatria row from 682; the Unified Silla infobox lists Munmu (661-681) then Sinmun (681-692).

wars.name: Conquest of Gaya
wars.outcome: Silla destroyed Takgitan Gaya (529), took Geumgwan Gaya (532) and Daegaya (562); the confederacy ended.
wars.note: The Gaya page also says the confederacy disintegrated under Goguryeo pressure between 391 and 412, which its own 532/562 dates contradict.

wars.name: Silla-Baekje campaign for the Han River valley
wars.outcome: Silla and Baekje took the valley from Goguryeo in 551; Silla took Baekje's half in late 553 and killed King Seong in 554.

wars.name: Silla-Tang conquest of Baekje
wars.outcome: Baekje ended in 660; Silla and Tang divided the occupation.

wars.name: Silla-Tang War

zones.text: the land south of the Taedong

wars.outcome: Silla victory: Tang left Baekje (671) and the land south of the Taedong (676); Tang recognised Silla's sovereignty there in 736.
wars.note: Chinese and Korean accounts of 674-675 differ; the page notes a Samguk Sagi figure of 200,000 Tang at Maeso (675) that it calls symbolic.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary; every frontier (Baekje, Goguryeo, Gaya, Tang-held Baekje) is approximate, and the east-coast extension to 40.1 N from 554 is unverified.
The line 'from the mouth of the Taedong River in the west to the East Korea Bay' is a described limit, not a surveyed one.

notes: Silla (378-681) and Unified Silla (682-935) are one kingdom; see the unified-silla notes. Cliopatria's Silla row has three jumps the pages explain: 534 (Geumgwan Gaya, 532), 555 (Han River valley, 553) and 567 (Daegaya, 562); each starts two to five years late, corrected as years-only verdicts. It has no shape for the Baekje land (671) or the land south of the Taedong (676): new keyframes silla_671 and silla_676, and silla_674 is marked wrong. The shape's reach to the east coast at 40.1 N from 555 is not on any page opened (the Silla page has Jinheung's campaigns 551-585 in the infobox only): unverified. Pages: 6 against a budget of 5 (Silla, Jinheung of Silla, Gaya confederacy, Silla-Tang War, Unified Silla, plus Tamna for the 662 tributary relation). No area on the Silla page (population only: 250,000 in 200, 1,000,000 in 660, 6,000,000 in 700, contradicting each other), so no infobox/Cliopatria comparison. Silla's vassalage under Goguryeo is on the pages ('Silla lost its status as a sovereign country becoming a vassal of Goguryeo', Silla page, no year; 'In 392, Silla formed an alliance with Goguryeo and became the vassal of Goguryeo', Naemul page; 'a vassal state of Goguryeo since Gwanggaeto defeated the Baekje and Wa troops invading Silla in 400', Jangsu page); it needs no event here because vassal events are written by the suzerain (goguryeo /ledger/20 and /31; the Goguryeo dossier dates it 400-468, the Naemul page 392). The 468 and 489 losses are written here (fix round), mirroring goguryeo /ledger/30 and /33; the 427 alliance with Baekje (Nulji) and the 540s-550s Gaya-Baekje diplomacy change no border. Mismatch with the Goguryeo dossier: it records Silla's gain of the whole Han River valley from Goguryeo in 553; the Jinheung page has Silla and Baekje taking it from Goguryeo in 551 and Silla taking Baekje's half in 553; both are recorded here. The Gaya dossier dates the Gaya losses 532 and 562 as here. Tang's dossier should carry the matching 676 contest_end and the 671 loss of the Baekje land. Gazetteer: nothing missing here. Fix round (2026-10-19): (1) losses to Goguryeo in 468 (Gangwon edge, same region as goguryeo /ledger/30) and 489 (northern frontier strip of North Gyeongsang, narrower than goguryeo /ledger/33, which takes the whole province inside Silla's outline), new keyframes silla_468, silla_489, silla_532, and a confidence-1 regain in 551 (no page dates it); silla_378 and silla_534 become years-only adjustments. The goguryeo author must narrow /ledger/33, draw the land in its own keyframes for 468-550 and add a 551 loss, otherwise the land is nobody's on the map for those years. (2) The 551 gain no longer includes Gyeonggi. (3) The 660 quotes are the Unified Silla page's own sentences. Not changed: silla_555's east-coast reach to 40.1 N, still on no page (Three Kingdoms of Korea, Silla, Jinheung pages silent); the 378 found event, still a bridge. Pages opened in the fix round: Jangsu of Goguryeo, Naemul of Silla, Three Kingdoms of Korea, Silla, Jinheung of Silla, Unified Silla.
